To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) trade can be used to promote economic growth, (2) trade can be utilized to reduce income inequality, (3) trade can be a means to increase employment opportunities in developing countries, and (4) the effectiveness of trade in achieving the above objectives is dependent on the nature of trade policies and the constraints faced by the economy in question.
trade liberalisation and redistribution are complementary to each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interrelationships between economic growth, income equality and trade.
the impact of the trade regime on the distribution of income in a developing country.
the following questions: (1) How does trade affect the growth of employment?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
trade, growth and equality can be mutually reinforcing in developing countries such India.
the trade policies of the developing countries have not been very effective in reducing inequality of income distribution.
the trade policies have not been able to achieve their objectives in terms of economic growth and income distribution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
export promotion is the best strategy for India in terms of both growth and redistribution.
trade policies can be used as an instrument of growth and employment generation and thereby of income equality.
trade is a very important factor in the development of the economy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
export promotion and redistribution are complementary strategies to achieve the goal of economic growth as well as to reduce income inequality.
a strategy of export promotion is likely to be more effective in reducing income inequality and in generating employment in developing countries.
trade can be an effective strategy for achieving both growth and income redistribution if it is not accompanied by a policy of import substitution.
